dcm2niix: interactive BIDS curation: acquisition labels and fieldmap associations are user decisions; upstream dcm2niix supplies the converter command line
surfannotate: interactive surface annotation: every result is a manual choice in the viewer
zarro: interactive OME-Zarr viewer: it has no batch output
nesvor: needs CUDA; its standalone form is the neurodesk-compute server
dicomview: interactive DICOM browser: dcm2niix and dicompare already ship as command lines
pipeline-builder: writes NeuroFlow workflows: neuroflow-mcp runs and validates them from the command line
dwicorrect: exes/dwi/shoreline builds the shoreline command line on the same core; its release packaging follows the app
fastprep: exes/fastprep drives separately installed niimath, brainchop, greedy-rs, synthsr, topofit and glm; a bundled release waits on packaging those (TopoFit licence pending)
me-ica: its meica CLI is released from niivue/meica-rs; no release is tagged yet
ants-denoise: ANTs ships DenoiseImage as its own command line: the Standalone dialog lists the Neurodesk ANTs container, whose DenoiseImage gives the app's voxels with one thread and the same options
brainqcnet: the authors publish BrainQCNet as a BIDS app container: the Standalone dialog lists garciaml/brainqcnetcpu 1.0.1, whose tables the app reproduces byte for byte (packages/brainqcnet/validation)
brainchop: Browser TensorFlow.js inference with WebGL; no command-line package.
stardist: Python StarDist (pip install stardist) is the command-line reference the app reproduces label for label on the example; no separate command line is packaged
calcium-imaging: no command-line package yet: v1 runs its pipeline (src/core) in browser workers only; CaImAn and Suite2p are the established command-line tools for batch work
spot-detection: the detector is a JavaScript port of Big-FISH, whose Python package (pip install big-fish) is the batch tool: on the example it gives the app's spot set and threshold; a packaged command line for the port is not done yet
gliomoda: the Neurocontainers gliomoda 0.0.4 image is the command-line reference: the Standalone dialog lists it, and packages/gliomoda/validation holds the app's labels to its outputs on the example
neuromorph: NeuroM, whose definitions the app follows, is the command-line route for batch morphometrics (pip install neurom); NeuroMorph has no packaged command line of its own yet
stitching: no command-line package yet: v1 runs its pipeline (src/core) in browser workers only; Fiji's Grid/Collection stitching and BigStitcher are the established command-line tools for batch work
structure-tensor: browser-only v1: the numerics (apps/structure-tensor/src/tensor.js) are DOM-free and Node-tested, but no command-line package is released yet
deconvolution: no command line yet: the Rust core in exes/deconvolution and the committed WebAssembly module in packages/deconvolution are ready to package through exes/node-cli in a later release
